items.label: text
items.text: A completeexplanationofcolour,or absenceofcolour,in aqueoussolutionsofmetalionsisquite complicated.However,thefollowing explanation should helpyou tounderstand thebasics.Wewill use an aqueous solution containingcopper(Il)ions as an example.

items.label: text
items.text: An aqueous solution of zinc sulfate is colourless, but an aqueous solution of copper(Il) sulfate is blue. As the sulfate ion is present in both solutions we can assume that any difference in colour is caused by the zinc ions and the copper(Il) ions. Zinc and copper are next to each other in the Periodic Table, so why should copper,but not zinc,form coloured ions?

items.text: The electronic configurations of the Zn2+ and Cu²+ ions are shown in fig D in the electrons-in-boxes format.
